newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Placer eyes 5 mln oz-plus gold mines.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Placer eyes 5 mln oz-plus gold mines.

text.p: Placer Dome Inc said on Wednesday it is spending about US$120 million a year searching for gold desposits of five million ounces or more.

"We're not spending any money on finding deposits under five million ounces," Placer Dome's president John Willson said after addressing a gold industry conference. "We are spending about US$120 million right now."

Placer Dome, which last month lost a bid to held develop the giant Busang gold desposit in Indonesia, one of the world's largest untapped gold resources, is looking as far afield as Chile, Australia, the U.S. and Canada, Willson said.
Earlier, Willson said gold exploration has become more competitive.
"There have been huge growths during this decade in the number of countries opening up to exploration," Willson said.
Developing countries offered exploration opprotunites, including Russia and those of Asia, Willson said.
Africa was also displaying exploration opportunities, he said.
"The old white mans grave, the Gold Coast of Ghana, is again the centre of excitement along with all the other West African countries which have traditionally been gold producers," Willson said.
Placer currently produces about two million ounces of gold a year, a figure it hopes to boost to 2.7 million ounces starting in the 1998-2000 time frame, Willson said.
The company's strategy was to produce gold from a smaller number of lower cost, longer life mines, Willson said.
Willson said Placer holds a positive view for gold, saying the current downturn in price only reflected a period weakness.
"We expect gold to trade in the US$360-US$400 (an ounce) range...we use US$375 for our long term planning," Willson said.
